Copies of selected TRForge modules (MIT licensed, see LICENSE), verbatim
but for three comment passages of Trg.h this project left out (below).

DO NOT EDIT THESE FILES beyond such a left-out passage. The first three
header lines of a TRForge module carry a hidden signature (an acrostic);
reformatting destroys it. Anything this project needs differently is
written in our own wrappers under TOMB5\specific\hd\, never in here.

Source : TROne's own vendor copy of TRForge (TROne, GPLv3, by Todesengel1931 -
         https://github.com/todesengel1931), which states: TRForge_Remastered,
         remastered 030ed51fed4f73914bd91c36ed9a7598ea9da711, 2026-08-31
Taken  : 2026-09-05, for #123 stage S0 (HD at run time)
Files  : 5

    src\trf_core\trf_types.h      shared scalar types and result codes
    src\trf_core\trf_file.h       whole-file helpers
    src\trf_core\trf_file.c       ditto
    src\trf_remaster\Trg.h        LEVELn.TRG - the remaster's room geometry
    src\trf_remaster\Trg.cpp      ditto

SHA-256, first 12 hex digits, over each file as git stores it (LF line ends;
a checkout may add CRs). On the day of the copy, 2026-09-05, all five were
identical to TROne's own copy (both sides hashed, byte counts equal):

    trf_types.h  680FA5F01431   1290 bytes
    trf_file.h   E3480EA66570    668 bytes
    trf_file.c   74686DFB52C4   1801 bytes
    Trg.h        7046FEA1D02C   8395 bytes
    Trg.cpp      12A20F61ACB8  10593 bytes

Edited here since, in Trg.h only, three comment passages left out, each
with a one-line note in its place where a note is needed: the passage over
the normal bytes (2026-10-04), the one over the vertex layout and the one
over the point lights (2026-10-06). Each told in words what the Remaster's
renderer does with a field; nothing of TRForge's code or byte layout
changed. Trg.h now:

    Trg.h        26F169147619   7063 bytes

The other four are unchanged. TROne has patched three files of its own
TRForge copy since 2026-09-05 (its vendor\trforge\PATCHES.md); none of that
is in this copy.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN, and why

    Dds.cpp / Dds.h        we have our own BC7 decoder, specific\bc7.cpp,
                           which the diagnostic tool DdsProbe already proves.
    ItemModels.h / .cpp    the .TRM reader. Its header includes
                           trf_level\Level.h (for bind_level_items) and
                           trf_remaster\Remaster.h, so a verbatim copy drags
                           in the whole trf_level branch - which #123's plan
                           rules out. The .TRM side therefore lives in our
                           own translation unit, specific\hd\hd_trm.cpp,
                           which credits TRForge for the format.
    Remaster.h / .cpp      same case: the header includes trf_assets\Image.h
                           and trf_remaster\Dds.h, the source includes
                           trf_level\Level.h and TrgTiles.h. The three parts
                           we need (install layout, LEVELn.MAP, sidecar
                           names) are a few dozen lines and are written in
                           specific\hd\hd_install.cpp and hd_bind.cpp.
    trf_level, trf_assets, trf_editor
                           not needed: our engine already holds the classic
                           level in memory, in its randomized state.

LANGUAGE STANDARD. Trg.cpp uses <filesystem>, so these files are compiled as
C++17 (per-file <LanguageStandard> in tomb5.vcxproj); the rest of the engine
keeps the project default. Nothing here crosses a translation unit boundary
with an STL type - specific\hd\hd_level.h is plain C-shaped on purpose.
